content: Neomycin, polymyxin, and bacitracin ophthalmic ointment is prescribed to treat infections of the eye and eyelid. These medications belong to a class of drugs known as antibiotics. They work by inhibiting the growth of bacteria that infect the surface of the eye. This medication is available as an ophthalmic ointment and is applied inside the lower eyelid of the affected eye. Typically, it is used every 3 to 4 hours for a duration of 7 to 10 days, as directed by your doctor. It is crucial to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Use the ointment exactly as prescribed, and do not use more or less of it or apply it more frequently than instructed. You should notice improvement in your eye or eyelid infection within the first few days of treatment. If your symptoms persist or worsen, contact your doctor. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve. Stopping the medication too early or skipping doses may result in incomplete treatment of the infection and could lead to bacterial resistance to antibiotics. This medication is intended for use in the eye only. Avoid letting it come into contact with your nose or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not share your tube of ointment with anyone, even if they have been prescribed the same medication, as this can spread infection. To apply the ointment, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. 2. Use a mirror or have someone assist you in applying the ointment. 3. Keep the ointment tube clean and avoid touching the tip to your eye, eyelid, fingers, or any other surface. 4. Lie down or tilt your head back while standing and look upward. 5. Hold the tube between your thumb and index finger, positioning it close to your eyelid without touching it. 6. Use the index finger of your other hand to pull down your lower eyelid, creating a pocket. 7. Squeeze the prescribed amount of ointment into the pocket formed by your lower eyelid. 8. Replace and tighten the cap immediately after use. 9. Gently close your eyes and keep them closed for 1 to 2 minutes to allow the medication to be absorbed. 10. Wipe away any excess ointment from the outside or below your eye with a clean tissue. Clean the outside of the tube with a tissue as well. 11. Wash your hands again to remove any residual ointment. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to neomycin, polymyxin, bacitracin, aminoglycoside antibiotics (e.g., amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, paromomycin, streptomycin, tobramycin), zinc, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of hearing problems or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: Eye pain Irritation, burning, itching, swelling, or redness of the eye or eyelid Worsening eye discharge Red or scaly patches around the eye or eyelid Rash Hives Difficulty breathing or swallowing Swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs Hoarseness Chest tightness Faintness or dizziness If you experience any unusual problems while using this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course of this medication, contact your doctor.
